newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Johannesburg's inner-city renewal project, launched on Thursday, was part of a broader development strategy to diversify economic activity which had until now depended on the exploitation of diminishing natural resources, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said.
- Financial information provider I-Net, part of Times Media Ltd, said it would form a joint venture with Bridge Information Systems, the U.S.-based global news group.
- The KWV wine cooperative said it would not ask the Cape High Court to keep confidential a forensic audit of its assets submitted to the court this week.
- Transport Minister Mac Maharaj and Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said three groups had been short-listed to advise the government on restructuring the Airports Company.
- The "truth commission" would hold a public hearing into the role of the business sector under apartheid, commissioners decided.
- The National Party lost control of its local government "flagship", when 10 members of the Pretoria city council resigned to join Roelf Meyer's New Movement Process.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The restructuring of unlisted African Bank has been completed but has resulted in the departure of almost the entire original management team.
- Electronic Measurements, a joint venture between Spescom and Plessey Tellumat, has successfully defended a challenge to the patents it holds over numeric pre-paid elctricity meters.
- Macmed Health Care said it had secured a strategic alliance with GE Medical Systems that would boost the fast-growing local medical equipment supplier's X-ray business to about 500 million rand.
SAKE-BEELD
- Housing prices again showed a real decline in the quarter to end-June and have now failed to keep track with the inflation rate for nine successive quarters -- since the start of 1995.
- A black-controlled computer supplier is demanding the cancellation of a contract awarded by Telkom to Sourcecom Technology Systems, alleging irregularities in the tender process.
- Efforts to end the strike in the sugar industry failed on Thrusday when workers rejected a tentative agreement betwen labour unions and employers.
- Labour federation Cosatu has asked the African National Congress to explain its position on proposed legislation on basic employment conditions.
THE STAR
- A passerby who stopped to help at an apparent accident outside Johannesburg was shot dead by members of of a gang trying to hijack a security van.
- A serial rapist wanted by police for the rapes of last six young women committed suicide on Thursday, also killing a teenager believed to have been his last victim.
